Do I have to use the SPD?
heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?

content_blocks.text: Buyers must issue an SPD for procurement exercises over the threshold (Route 3) and it is recommended that it is also used for all Route 2 procurements.
heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?

content_blocks.text: The SPD can be used as part of either a single stage or multi-stage procedure.
heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?

heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?
Does each member of a consortium need to fill in a separate SPD or can the lead consortium member complete one on behalf of all?

content_blocks.text: Yes, all members of the consortium need to fill in a separate SPD response. The lead consortium member should return this to the buyer along with their SPD response.

heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?

Why aren’t there questions on equality and health and safety?

content_blocks.text: Equality and Health and Safety are not listed as selection criteria in the Public Contracts Scotland Regulations 2015, therefore they have not been created as standard questions.

How do I shortlist?

content_blocks.text: Shortlisting in the SPD allows a buyer to rank responses and this is done within the Technical and Professional Ability section. This will allow the buyer to determine who should be shortlisted and taken forward into the next stage of the procurement exercise.

How do I shortlist?

content_blocks.text: How you will ‘shortlist’ bidders must be detailed in the Contract Notice . This should include weighting and scoring information and methodology. These criteria must be objective and non-discriminatory .

content_blocks.text: How should I handle SPDs for framework agreements and Dynamic Purchasing Systems (DPS) after Brexit?
heading_path: Do I have to use the SPD?

How should I handle SPDs for framework agreements and Dynamic Purchasing Systems (DPS) after Brexit?

content_blocks.text: If your framework or DPS was launched before the end of the transition period from the EU you should continue to use the ESPD request you created for that procurement exercise, even if that means issuing the ESPD request after the end of the transition period. The original ESPD request will still be attached to your original contract notice so there will be no need to create another request.
